dataformats.q: A customer's names appear as 'MÃ¼ller' and 'CafÃ©'. What is the most likely cause?
options: The database column is too short for the names
UTF-8 bytes were decoded as Windows-1252 or Latin-1
The file was compressed and not unzipped properly
The names were typed in with the wrong keyboard layout
dataformats.why: That pattern of a capital A with a mark before another symbol is the classic sign of UTF-8 bytes read with a one-byte Western encoding.

dataformats.q: Why should you store timestamps in UTC?
options: UTC values take less space on disk than local times
Databases cannot store any other time zone
UTC is the local time of most cloud data centres
UTC avoids daylight saving gaps and repeats, so every moment has one value
dataformats.why: UTC has no daylight saving changes, so each moment maps to exactly one value; you convert to local time only for display.

dataformats.q: A UK supplier sends dates like 03/04/2026 and your US colleague loads them with default settings. What do you do first?
options: Confirm the format is day first and parse it with an explicit format string
Nothing, date parsers detect the country automatically
Convert every date to Unix time before checking anything
Ask the supplier to switch to Excel serial numbers
dataformats.why: 03/04/2026 is 3 April in the UK and 4 March in the US. Confirm the format and parse it explicitly instead of relying on a default.

dataformats.q: An ops team wants the order number pulled out of a free-text reference like 'paid ref ORD-004417 thanks'. Best approach?
options: Split the text on spaces and take the third word
An LLM call for every row, with no checks on the output
A tested regex such as ORD-\d{6} using search, with misses sent to review
Ask users to retype all old references by hand
dataformats.why: A small regex tested on real examples extracts the ID reliably and cheaply, and a review queue catches the forms it misses.

dataformats.q: Spot the mistake: 'I open Excel exports with errors="replace" so the pipeline never crashes on encoding.'
options: It is fine, because replacement characters are removed later
It hides lost characters, so names and addresses are silently corrupted
It only works for CSV files and not for JSON files
It makes the pipeline slower but is otherwise correct
dataformats.why: Replacing undecodable bytes turns real characters into placeholders without warning. Decode with the right encoding and fail loudly on errors.

options: Storing the project's secrets and API tokens
Recording the exact versions installed on one machine
Describing the project, its dependencies and tool settings
Holding the test results from the last CI run
pytooling.why: pyproject.toml is the standard project description file. Exact installed versions live in a lock file, and secrets never belong in the repo.

pytooling.q: Why commit a lock file for an application?
options: It records exact versions so every install matches what was tested
It makes Python run the code faster
It stops other people from changing the code
It replaces the need for a virtual environment
pytooling.why: Version ranges allow new releases to slip in. The lock file pins every library, including indirect ones, so installs are repeatable.

pytooling.q: A job fails with 'No module named pydantic' on the server, though you installed it. What do you check first?
options: Reinstall Python on the server from scratch
Whether pydantic has released a new major version
The server's CPU and memory usage
Which interpreter runs the job, by printing sys.executable
pytooling.why: The library is usually installed in a different environment from the one the scheduler uses. sys.executable shows which Python is really running.

pytooling.q: A customer's repo has 2,000 mypy errors under strict mode. What is a sensible plan?
options: Turn mypy off because the codebase is too old
Start with default settings, fix real errors, then make new modules strict
Add # type: ignore to every line that has an error
Rewrite the whole codebase before shipping any feature
pytooling.why: Gradual adoption keeps the tool useful. Strict settings go first to new or critical modules, and the strict area grows over time.

pytooling.q: Spot the mistake: 'I put the API token in settings.py as a default value so the job always works.'
options: Secrets in code end up in git history; read them from the environment
Nothing, defaults make the program easier to run
The token should be in pyproject.toml instead
Tokens should be logged at start-up so you can debug them
pytooling.why: Anything in source code is copied to every clone and stays in git history. Read secrets from the environment or a secrets store and never log them.

entnetwork.q: What does TLS inspection on a corporate proxy do?
options: It blocks every HTTPS site that is not on an allowlist
It speeds up HTTPS by caching certificates
It converts HTTPS traffic to plain HTTP inside the network
It decrypts traffic and re-encrypts it with the company's own CA
entnetwork.why: The proxy opens the encrypted traffic to scan it and re-signs it with a corporate certificate authority, which your program must then trust.

options: Turning the proxy off for every request
Listing hosts that should be reached directly, without the proxy
Blocking hosts that the proxy refuses to reach
Storing the proxy's username and password
entnetwork.why: NO_PROXY lists internal hosts and domains that must bypass the proxy, such as localhost and internal services.

entnetwork.q: Your Python client gets CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED inside a bank, while the browser works. What do you do first?
options: Check the certificate issuer, then trust the corporate root CA in your bundle
Set verify=False until the pilot is over
Ask the bank to turn off its proxy for your server
Switch from HTTPS to HTTP for the model API
entnetwork.why: The browser trusts the corporate CA through the OS store, and Python uses its own bundle. Adding the corporate root fixes it safely.

entnetwork.q: You need a customer's servers to call two vendor APIs. How should you ask for firewall access?
options: Ask for general internet access for the AI servers
Send the vendor's marketing page and ask IT to work it out
List sources, hostnames, port 443, direction, purpose, data and an owner
Wait until go-live week so the rules are fresh
entnetwork.why: Specific, written requests with hostnames, ports, sources and purpose get approved much faster than vague ones, and should be sent early.

entnetwork.q: Spot the mistake: 'curl works on the host, so the network is fine for my container too.'
options: Correct, containers always share the host's network settings
curl results only apply to Windows machines
The container needs a VPN of its own for every request
Containers may lack the host's proxy variables and trusted CAs
entnetwork.why: A container starts with its own environment and trust store. Pass the proxy variables in, add the CA bundle, and test with curl inside the container.

poc.q: What is the main difference between a POC and a pilot?
options: A POC tests if it can work; a pilot tests value with real users
A POC is always paid and a pilot is always free
A pilot is shorter than a POC and uses sample data
They are the same thing with different names
poc.why: A POC answers feasibility on sample or historical data. A pilot puts it in front of real users in daily work, usually paid and longer.

poc.q: What does 'fixed time, variable scope' mean for a POC?
options: The end date moves if the work takes longer
Scope is fixed and the team works overtime to finish
The end date holds, and lower-priority scope is dropped if needed
The customer can add scope at any time without changes
poc.why: The time box protects the decision date. Ranking scope in advance makes it quick to decide what to drop.

poc.q: A prospect wants a POC next week but cannot say what happens if it succeeds. What do you do?
options: Start anyway, since any POC builds goodwill
Ask who decides and what next step success leads to, before agreeing
Offer a longer free trial so they have more time
Send a price list and wait for them to call back
poc.why: Without a decision maker and a next step, a POC tends to drift. Clarify the decision and budget first, or propose a short discovery instead.

poc.q: An RFP asks if your product runs fully on-premises. It does not. How do you answer?
options: Mark it compliant and sort out the details later
Skip the question so it does not lower your score
Say it is on the roadmap to keep the deal alive
Mark it not compliant and describe the nearest alternative precisely
poc.why: RFP answers often become contract terms. An honest 'not compliant' with a clear alternative is safer and usually more credible.

poc.q: Spot the mistake: 'We planned the POC as 40 engineer-days of building work for our 40-day team.'
options: Nothing, it uses the team's time efficiently
POCs should never be estimated in engineer-days
No time is left for waiting on access, data and reviews
The team is too large for any POC
poc.why: Waiting on access and approvals often takes a large share of a first engagement. Plan a buffer and state your assumptions.
